courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Macroeconomics, international economics and economic policy
Business economics, accounting, finance, strategy and marketing
Mathematics, statistics, econometrics, data analysis and independent research
Public economics, welfare, inequality and applied social policy
Digitalisation, data and technology in the economy
Economic philosophy, ethics and the history of economic ideas
adjacent: Behavioural and health economics, psychology and consumer decision-making
questions: How can data and empirical methods answer economic and business questions?
How can economic analysis inform social, welfare and health decisions?

trace: Develops financial and management accounting,financial-statement interpretation,costing,budgeting and discounted-cash-flow investment appraisal. It directly supports corporate financial decisions,without providing a complete specialist financial-economics sequence.
examines the economic and managerial consequences of AI and technological change

Direct securities/bond/stock/derivative pricing,interest-rate risk andtermstructure,bank balance-sheet/capital/liquidity/risk decisions,monetarypolicy andfinancialcrises. Excel-basedbankmanagementsimulation and research-articleextension add substantivefinancialanalysis,not merely budgeting.
provides foundational microeconomic and macroeconomic analysis of markets, firms, households and the wider economy
Develops macroeconomic short/medium/long-run models,expectations,open-economy andfiscal/monetary policy using algebra,graphs andindicators; no unverified dedicatedtrade-theory sequence asserted.
develops advanced microeconomic analysis of choice under uncertainty, firms and markets
examines market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation, redistribution and government intervention
provides econometric tools for causal and predictive analysis of economic data
examines biases, heuristics and framing in economic decision-making
Specific complementary product-development work translates customer needs into design, production, cost/proceeds and sustainability decisions. It is not an additional economics theory course.
examines marketing strategy, consumer behaviour and customer engagement
develops business strategy and responsible digital transformation from analysis to execution
develops applied market research through data gathering, analysis and managerial recommendations

Direct internationaltrade theories,FDI,foreignexchange andmonetarysystem study withininternationalbusiness,plusgovernance,trade-policy andgametheoretic tariff analysis. This is a partial economicrelationship,withfirm/market-entry emphasis.

Specific complementary venture creation through design thinking, market validation and business planning. Its business-prerequisite role is not the substantive justification; those actual operating decisions contribute to the business strand.
provides research design, sampling, statistics and empirical analysis for economic and business questions
examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structure through organisational psychology
develops negotiation, strategic interaction, framing and the psychology of influence
develops data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation for empirical economic and business analysis
adds predictive modelling and machine learning for data-driven economic and business analysis
provides calculus and differential-equation foundations for quantitative economic modelling
provides probability, estimation, inference and simulation foundations for quantitative economic analysis

Specific complementary normative theories andphilosophical argument support evaluation of economic andfinancial responsibilities; no prescribedwealth/poverty case orhistory-of-economics sequence inferred.
introduces epidemiological study design, population health, disease risk and evidence for public-health decisions

Direct psychological and neuroscientific foundations of behaviour and mental processes, plus methods and brain-function knowledge needed for health psychology. Neural content is complementary to economic decision inquiry, not economic theory.
provides social-psychological analysis of attitudes, influence and group behaviour relevant to consumer and economic choices

Actual experimentaldesign andmultivariable models for health/behavioural group,categorical andlatent-variable questions,withdiagnostics,R/RCommander,analysispapers andposter. Specific empirical-method contribution; no econometric-equivalence claim.
Direct study of biopsychosocial determinants of health, stress, illness and health behaviour; a specific complementary health-domain contribution, not economic evaluation of healthcare.

Direct systematic review and meta-analysis with effect sizes and hands-on R supports evidence synthesis about behaviour and health and evidence-based policy. It is not a substitute for econometric impact evaluation.

Programming enables implementation,testing andexplanation of computational economic andfinancial models; actual structuredPython anddata collections are the complementary method,not a guaranteed finance project.

Linear systems,matrixmethods,least-squares,eigenvalues,quadraticforms andSVD support multivariable economic/financial models andstatisticalestimation. Complementary mathematical foundations,not a specialisedfinance syllabus.

Numerical roots,quadrature,differentialequations andlinear/nonlinear systems,error/stability analysis supply concrete solution/validation methods for quantitative economic models. Financial applications are not claimed as prescribed coursework.

Probability,Bayesian inference,expectedutility,temporalmodels,Markovdecisionprocesses andbandits develop formal decisions underuncertainty,complementing financialrisk/economicchoice; intelligentagent rather than finance setting.

Actual heuristic/local/global optimisation,first/secondorder methods,linear/discrete optimisation andimplementation support constrained quantitative decision models. Complementary computational methods,not dedicatedportfolio theory.

Matrix/Fourier computation,greedy/dynamicprogramming andnetworkflows plus experimental algorithm evaluation support efficient quantitative modelimplementation. Broad algorithms remain complementary to economic/financial inquiry,not a replacement for finance theory.

alternatives.label: Economics, business & data
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum is broader than pure economics: it combines micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisational study, data science, econometrics and international business.
alternatives.concept: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and public policy are combined with business strategy, accounting, financial decisions, marketing, organisational behaviour and empirical data analysis.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.
traceOverrides: Actual experimentaldesign andmultivariable models for health/behavioural group,categorical andlatent-variable questions,withdiagnostics,R/RCommander,analysispapers andposter. Specific empirical-method contribution; no econometric-equivalence claim.

alternatives.label: Economics, psychology & health decisions
alternatives.labelReason: The programme combines economics with behavioural science, consumer and organisational decisions, health psychology and evidence methods. It does not claim dedicated health-economics training.
alternatives.concept: Economics and empirical methods are combined with psychology, consumer and organisational decisions, public health and research synthesis to study human choices and health-related behaviour.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad economics/business option, six courses change: psychology and brain/behaviour foundations, health psychology, population-health evidence, negotiation and research synthesis replace mathematical probability/calculus, AI-economy study, international business, product development and practical finance. These changes shift academic weight to behaviour, health determinants and evidence synthesis, while retaining a substantial economic and empirical core. Health psychology and epidemiology complement economics; they do not constitute a health-economics specialist sequence.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics & financial decisions
alternatives.labelReason: Mathematical, statistical and computational methods combine with economic models, accounting, investment appraisal, securities pricing and bank decisions. This describes related quantitative economics with finance; it does not promise a specialist financial-economics degree.
alternatives.concept: Mathematical and computational analysis of economic and financial decisions, combining probability, numerical methods, econometrics and optimisation with accounting, securities and banking, economic behaviour and business decisions.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.
alternatives.distinctness: Replaces broad marketing/product/organisational study with programming, linear algebra, numerical analysis, probabilistic decisions, optimisation and algorithmic models. The financial-accounting/banking and economic core gives these methods an explicit quantitative economic/financial purpose. Unlike the health option, it does not organise inquiry around psychological mechanisms, clinical behaviour or population-health evidence.

routeSelection.route: Economics of Markets and Organisations major
routeSelection.basis: Generic IBEB target. Choose the broad analytical markets-and-organisations route rather than accounting, finance, health, marketing or geographic/sector specialisation: its organising territory spans firms, labour and markets. This is an academic judgment, not an official default. First listed eligible option Applied Game Theory is the neutral tie-break within its 4 EC elective choice. Compulsory courses and seminar are retained. Selection was independent of UCR match convenience.

selection.assessment: Three sequentially justified programmes: broad economic/business/data inquiry; psychology/health andevidence synthesis; quantitative economic/financial decisions. Fresh actual pricing/banking/investment andempirical econometric content corrects the earlier narrow practical-finance assessment. The third changes mathematical/computational priorities rather than adding a finance title to the broad business set. Its methods support concrete modelling/uncertainty/estimation tasks without claiming finance-specific projects. Pairwise course/EC floors andqualitative differences pass. Accountingalone has onlyone dedicated accountingcourse andcannot sustain a furtheraccounting/reporting route;urban/port/transport topic lacks sustaineddocumenteddomainimplementation. Existingmarket/organisation,international andpublicpolicy directions remain covered by broad economics. Maximumthree;no fourth manufactured.

blocks: Both address public economic questions. UCR explicitly covers market failure, taxation, spending and redistribution; a dedicated healthcare-economics syllabus is not established.
The comparator contains a dedicated History of Economic Thought course. UCR does not add an unrelated history course merely to imitate this component.

Both study finance. UCR explicitly includes securities pricing, interest-rate risk and banking decisions, with algebraic analysis and a bank simulation; it does not reproduce the full specialist external finance sequence.
Market Research provides applied research design, data collection and analysis for business questions, but is not the same as the programme-wide Research Project.
Direct partial relationship in business strategy and transformation. This does not reproduce the external combined organisation-and-strategy syllabus.

Both address international trade, foreign investment, exchange and monetary systems. UCR applies these within firm strategy and governance; this is a partial international-economic relationship, not an identical theory syllabus.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistics and empirical research foundations, but is broader than Applied Statistics 1.

Both develop applied statistical modelling and inference. UCR frames multivariable, categorical and latent-variable analyses within health and behavioural research; identical syllabuses are not asserted.

UCR studies expected utility and strategic multi-agent decisions, including negotiation, auctions and voting. This is a partial game- and decision-theory relationship; it does not reproduce the external combined mathematics and game-theory course.
Partial relationship through ethical theory and evaluation. The external philosophy course is not reduced to ethics alone.

Both support research questions, academic sources and written/oral argument. UCR also includes personal and civic formation; the external 4 EC Academic Skills unit includes four internal skills/project activities, not four extra credited courses.
The comparator requires an individual 10-EC thesis. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so UCR's optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.

notes.text: The Erasmus curriculum provides a longer fixed economics-and-business sequence, a formal major with a seminar and an individual thesis. The UCR options offer substantial economics with different business, behavioural and health-related combinations. They do not reproduce specialist accounting, financial or health-economics training, the full selected major or the required thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: The English-taught International Bachelor Economics and Business Economics at Erasmus School of Economics combines economic theory, business economics and quantitative methods. Students complete a major, a seminar and an individual thesis. This comparison shows one permitted 2026–2027 pathway with the Economics of Markets and Organisations major and a 12-EC minor.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option combines economics and public policy with business strategy, accounting, financial decisions, marketing and data. The second adds psychology, health-related behaviour and evidence synthesis. The third gives more space to mathematical and computational analysis alongside accounting, securities, banking and economic decisions. These are related programmes with different priorities; they do not reproduce every specialist major, the seminar or the required thesis. Shared rows show partial curricular relationships.
